headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and certain distribution infrastructure investments onto large energy users, primarily data centers, to reduce residential electricity bills and extend energy assistance programs.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Senator Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (initially), customer advocates, lawmakers aiming to save residential electricity customers money.
opponents: Governor Abigail Spanberger (due to amendments weakening original intent), data centers and large manufacturers.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Data Center Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger proposed amendments to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aimed to shift energy costs to data centers, with critics arguing her changes weakened the original intent to save residential customers money. Lawmakers ultimately accepted some of her amendments, impacting the extent of cost shifting.

headline: Require Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water users supplying data centers report monthly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board to inform rezoning and special use permit decisions.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups like The Piedmont Environmental Council and Virginia Conservation Network, community advocates.
opponents: Not explicitly stated in provided information.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Pass Data Center Water Reporting Bill
news_summary: Virginia's legislature passed SB 553, requiring utilities to report data center water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board. This aims to provide communities with clearer insight into local resource use, which has often been private.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) like data centers, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Thomas, community advocates concerned about noise and environmental impacts, environmental groups like The Piedmont Environmental Council and Virginia Conservation Network.
opponents: Data center industry (as it imposes new requirements and potential restrictions).
news_headline: Virginia Enacts Data Center Siting and Noise Laws
news_summary: HB 153, now law, introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments for noise on nearby homes and schools. It also allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, providing a foundation for stronger future regulations.
